newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money inactive, gilts yields steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money inactive, gilts yields steady.

text.p: The Indian money market ended a quiet day on Friday with call money quoted in the 0.10-0.50 percent range while security prices remained largely steady in limited trade, dealers said.

They said there were only quotes for overnight money and no deals were struck on Friday as it was the reporting day when banks report positions to the Reserve Bank of India. Banks do not borrow on reporting days as it increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.
Dealers said three-day money was traded in the 6.0-7.0 percent range, indicating that call money would open Saturday around 10 percent. They said 14-day repos was done at 10.5 percent.
Prices of government securities were steady in poor trade, dealers said. Volumes on the National Stock Exchange were around 500 million rupees on Friday against Thursday's one billion, they said.

The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock traded on Friday at 101.59 rupees against Thrsday's 101.65, they said. The 14.0 percent 2006 was traded at 102.10 rupees against Thursday's 102.11, they added.
Certificates of deposit maturing in January 1997 yielded 10.88 percent against last trade of 10.90 percent, dealers said.
